title: Senate Passes Sweeping Energy Permitting Bill in 62-33 Vote
dek: The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act would speed approvals for power plants, transmission lines, mines and data centers, and now faces an uncertain future in the House.

title: White House Fires National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross After Week of Tech Outages
dek: Sean Cairncross is out after little more than a year in the Senate-confirmed role, and Pentagon technology chief Kirsten Davies will take over in an acting capacity.

title: Trump Gives Posthumous Pardon to Baseball Hit King Pete Rose
dek: The pardon wipes away the tax convictions of the sport's all-time hits leader, who died in 2024 still barred from the Hall of Fame.

title: Texas Execution of Reinaldo Dennes Takes Over an Hour as Staff Struggle to Find a Vein
dek: Reinaldo Dennes, 70, cried out in pain during a 63-minute lethal injection in Huntsville, weeks after Tennessee's failed execution of Christa Pike put the method under fresh scrutiny.

title: Atmospheric River Floods California, Breaks a 108-Year San Francisco Rain Record
dek: The season's first big atmospheric river swamped Bay Area streets, forced Los Angeles to warn burn-scar neighborhoods to prepare to evacuate, and dumped heavy snow in the Sierra.

title: Russia Hits Kyiv Bridges in Massive Overnight Barrage Hours After Trump Calls Putin ‘Tired’ and Ready for a Deal
dek: More than 400 drones and 110 missiles struck Ukraine overnight, killing at least eight people, knocking out power as temperatures fall below zero, and spilling into Polish airspace.

title: Britain to Give Ukraine More Than 1,000 Long-Range Strike Drones in £260 Million Package
dek: Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced the package in Berlin, where allies also discussed joining peace talks, as Russia steps up its winter campaign against Ukraine's power grid.

title: Young People Walk Out Across Europe in Coordinated Strike Over Living Costs and Military Spending
dek: Students in more than 25 countries walked out of school on Friday, demanding money for housing and education instead of weapons, as trade unions staged a general strike in Italy.

title: Iraqi Forces Move Into Kataib Hezbollah Stronghold in Deal to End Militia's Grip on Jurf al-Sakhar
dek: Government troops deployed in the town south of Baghdad on Friday under a compromise that lets the Iran-backed militia pull back rather than fight, after an investigation accused it of smuggling hundreds of millions of dollars in oil.

title: Pakistan Reports 22 Militants Killed in Two Days of Northwest Raids
dek: Security forces raided militant hideouts in South Waziristan, Bannu and Tank over two days, the military said, in the latest round of a counterterrorism campaign that has intensified across the northwest.

title: Senate Rejects Iran War Powers Resolution in 51-48 Vote, Backing Trump Weeks After Midterm Losses
dek: Senate Republicans defeated a measure directing President Donald Trump to end the war in Iran or seek Congress's approval, with three Republicans breaking ranks and one Democrat voting against it.

title: Incoming Oversight Chair Garcia Orders Trump Family and Top Officials to Preserve Records Ahead of Probes
dek: Rep. Robert Garcia sent a dozen letters to Vice President JD Vance, members of the Trump family, and current and former officials, mapping Democrats' investigation targets before they take control of Congress in January.

title: Trump Pressures Congress to Pass Farm Bill Before Democrats Take Control in January
dek: The president urged Republican majorities to finish the long-stalled five-year farm bill in the session's remaining days, warning farmers need certainty before the 2027 planting season.

title: Trump Says He Will Be 'Unbelievably Productive' With a Democratic Congress
dek: In a Fox News interview, the president said his veto power gives him leverage over the incoming Democratic majorities and predicted deals would follow his vetoes.

title: Lenovo Posts Record $30.2 Billion Quarter as AI Server Sales Nearly Triple
dek: Revenue jumped 48% in the September quarter, beating estimates, as demand for AI infrastructure pushed the company's server business to its strongest quarter ever.

title: Gap Cuts Annual Forecasts as Holiday Demand Starts Slow
dek: The apparel retailer lowered its full-year sales and profit outlook after a slow start to the holiday quarter, though third-quarter earnings still beat estimates.

title: Ross Stores Tops Third-Quarter Estimates but Signals a Slower Holiday Quarter
dek: The off-price retailer raised its full-year earnings outlook after a strong quarter, but held its holiday sales forecast steady, sending shares lower in extended trading.

title: Intuit to Sell Mailchimp for $3.68 Billion, Less Than a Third of What It Paid
dek: The TurboTax maker agreed to sell its email-marketing business to Bending Spoons as it sharpens its focus on AI, while cutting its full-year revenue outlook.

title: TSMC and Samsung Pause Some Chip Shipments to China Under New U.S. Export Rules
dek: The world's two largest contract chipmakers halted deliveries while they seek U.S. export licences, after Washington closed a loophole for Chinese chip designers.

title: Google Brings Gemini Computer Use to the Mac, Letting Its AI Click and Type for You
dek: Gemini can now work through multi-step tasks across Mac apps, local files and the web in a background window, putting Google in direct competition with the AI agents already living on the desktop.

title: European Commission Hit by AI-Assisted Cyberattack as Investigators Point to the Artex Tool
dek: Hackers disrupted the European Commission's staff HR and medical systems for more than ten days, and the EU's own cyber team says the attack highly likely involved Artex, an AI-powered hacking framework.

title: Microsoft Confirms Its November Windows 11 Hotpatch Can Stop Office and Other Apps From Launching
dek: The no-restart security update KB5132043 is breaking apps on enterprise PCs managed through Windows Autopatch, and Microsoft's temporary fix is a registry edit while a permanent repair is prepared.

title: Huawei Launches OSTA, Its First New Phone Brand Since Honor, With the Wide-Screen O1 Pro
dek: Six years after selling Honor, Huawei has a new smartphone sub-brand aimed at younger buyers who want AI features without flagship prices, starting with the O1 Pro in China.

title: Valve Opens Direct Sales of the 512GB Steam Machine as Memory Costs Squeeze the 2TB Model
dek: The entry-level Steam Machine can now be bought outright while supplies last, but Valve has closed the 2TB waitlist to new signups and says it does not know how many more units it can build or what they will cost.

title: HBO Renews The Gilded Age for Season 5 as Its Audience Keeps Growing
dek: The Julian Fellowes period drama earned an early fifth season midway through its fourth, with Season 4 averaging 5.9 million viewers an episode and tracking as the show's most-watched season yet.

title: Nikki Glaser to Star in a Scripted Netflix Series as the Streamer Launches Its New Comedy Studio
dek: Netflix has launched Netflix Is a Joke Studios, an in-house incubator for turning stand-up talent into scripted stars, and Glaser is its first partner, with a series and two specials on the way.

title: Larry Poindexter, Days of Our Lives and S.W.A.T. Actor, Dies at 66 Days After Being Hit by a Car
dek: The veteran character actor, whose career spanned more than four decades and 170 film and television credits, died suddenly in a Los Angeles hospital while awaiting surgery for broken ribs.

title: Macy's 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade Swaps Solo Broadway Numbers for One Big Medley
dek: For its landmark 100th march, the parade will feature a single ten-minute Broadway medley with performers from nine productions, introduced by Julianne Hough, plus a tribute to Dolly Parton.

title: Much Ado About Nothing Opens on Broadway as a Confetti-Soaked Dance Party
dek: Jamie Lloyd's production starring Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell opened at the Winter Garden Theatre on November 19, turning Shakespeare's comedy into a pink, pop-fueled rave that mostly won over the critics.

title: Lightning End Connor McDavid's 23-Game Point Streak in 3-1 Win Over Oilers
dek: Ilya Mikheyev's third-period goal proved the winner as Tampa Bay snapped Edmonton's six-game winning run and held the NHL's leading scorer off the scoresheet for the first time this season.

title: Knicks Survive Fourth-Quarter Collapse to Edge Timberwolves 102-99
dek: Karl-Anthony Towns scored 22 points against his former team as New York nearly squandered a 19-point lead in Minnesota before holding on for a third straight win.

title: Grizzlies Rout Short-Handed Warriors 126-98 for Fifth Straight Win
dek: Jaylen Wells scored 22 points and Memphis never trailed as Golden State finished a winless five-game road trip without the injured Stephen Curry.

title: Rams Star Puka Nacua Suspended Three Games for Personal Conduct Violation
dek: The NFL handed the Los Angeles wide receiver a three-game ban over a New Year's Eve incident, but he will serve it while on injured reserve and miss no extra time.

title: Kings Rally From Three Down to Beat Maple Leafs 4-3 in Shootout
dek: Adrian Kempe scored the only shootout goal as Los Angeles erased a 3-0 deficit in Toronto, handing the Maple Leafs an eighth straight defeat.

title: Court Freezes Venezuelan TPS Ruling Hours After Trump Administration's Third Supreme Court Bid
dek: The Justice Department's third emergency trip to the Supreme Court lasted a day: an appeals court froze the ruling that would have restored Venezuelan deportation protections, and the administration withdrew its request.

title: Judge Extends Block on Trump's Triumphal Arch for Two More Weeks
dek: U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan extended the restraining order blocking construction of the proposed 250-foot arch, keeping the project frozen until December 3 while she weighs a longer-term injunction.

title: Record Rain Floods South Florida, Closes Schools and Collapses a Synagogue Roof
dek: A slow-moving storm dumped 15.3 inches of rain on parts of Broward County in a single day, flooding roads and homes, collapsing the roof of a Hollywood synagogue and closing public schools across South Florida on Thursday.

title: White House Pulls FDA Nominee Heidi Overton on Eve of Senate Vote
dek: The White House pulled Dr. Heidi Overton's nomination to run the FDA on Tuesday, the day before a Senate committee vote, after bipartisan pushback over vaccines, abortion and vaping left her without the support to advance.

title: ICE Agents Pepper-Sprayed a Pregnant U.S. Citizen in Modesto. She Was Released Without Charges.
dek: Lizbeth Vargas Andrade, 23 and 12 weeks pregnant, says she was thrown to the ground, pepper-sprayed and held for about five hours outside the Stanislaus County jail. ICE says she interfered with an arrest.

title: Boston's Beloved CITGO Sign Lights Up Again Tonight, 30 Feet Higher Over Kenmore Square
dek: After six dark months, Boston's most famous sign returns on Thursday night, rebuilt and raised above the new towers crowding Kenmore Square.

title: World Court Rules Myanmar Committed Genocide Against the Rohingya
dek: The International Court of Justice ruled by nine votes to six that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya in 2017, the first time the court has ever found a state responsible for genocide.

title: Denmark's Parliament Ratifies Greenland Security Deal With the U.S. in 109-0 Vote
dek: Denmark's parliament voted 109-0 to ratify the security agreement with the United States over Greenland, clearing the final political hurdle for a deal aimed at ending the standoff over the Arctic island.

title: Houthi Missile Damages Riyadh's PIF Tower in Second Strike on Financial District
dek: A suspected Houthi missile struck the PIF Tower in Riyadh early Thursday, blowing out windows across seven to eight floors of the sovereign wealth fund's headquarters in the second attack on the financial district in under two weeks.

title: IAEA Says North Korea Has Built Another Extension to Its Yongbyon Enrichment Plant
dek: IAEA chief Rafael Grossi told the agency's 35-nation Board of Governors that North Korea built a further extension to its Yongbyon enrichment plant in September and October, calling the ongoing expansion a cause for serious concern.

title: Fiji Declares a National State of Disaster as El Niño Drought Drains Water Supplies
dek: Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka declared the nationwide emergency on Wednesday, unlocking FJ$20 million for water, farmers and remote island communities as dry conditions are forecast to last into April.

title: Trump, Xi and Putin Hold First-Ever Trilateral Summit in Shenzhen, Pledging Nuclear Talks and More Oil
dek: The leaders of the United States, China and Russia met for about 80 minutes in Shenzhen on Thursday, issuing a four-point declaration on nuclear risks, U.N. reform, oil supplies and the International Criminal Court — but with no breakthrough on Ukraine or Iran.

title: Hegseth Signs Military Cooperation Deal With Venezuela, Calling It a 'Compliant Security Partner'
dek: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a new U.S.-Venezuela military agreement in Caracas on Wednesday, ten months after American forces captured Nicolás Maduro, covering joint training, intelligence sharing and defense equipment.

title: House Democrats Nominate Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker in 251-11 Vote, Putting Him on the Brink of History
dek: House Democrats overwhelmingly chose Hakeem Jeffries as their nominee for speaker on Wednesday, putting the Brooklyn lawmaker in line to become the first Black speaker in U.S. history when the new Congress convenes on January 3.

title: Sanders Unveils Four-Year Medicare for All Plan as He Prepares to Retake the Senate Health Chair
dek: Sen. Bernie Sanders laid out a four-year path to universal health care on Wednesday, starting with lowering the Medicare eligibility age to 55, as he prepares to chair the Senate health committee when Democrats take control in January.

title: Senate Clears Final Hurdle for Sweeping Permitting Bill, Setting Up a Final Vote as Soon as Thursday Night
dek: The Senate voted 65-31 on Wednesday to end debate on the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, the biggest rewrite of federal permitting law in a generation, with a final passage vote expected Thursday night.

title: Anthropic Debuts on Nasdaq After Record $81 Billion IPO Values AI Lab at $1.5 Trillion
dek: The maker of the Claude chatbot begins trading Thursday under the ticker ANT after selling 980 million shares at $83 apiece — the largest initial public offering in history, eclipsing SpaceX's $75 billion debut.

title: Fed Minutes Show October Hold Was a 'Close Call' as Officials Lean Toward a December Hike
dek: Minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting, released Wednesday, show almost all policymakers expect further rate increases — and that some who backed holding rates steady viewed the decision as a close call.

title: Walmart Tops Third-Quarter Estimates and Raises Its Outlook as Holiday Shopping Nears
dek: The retail giant reported revenue of $188.8 billion for the quarter ended October 31, beating Wall Street's expectations, and lifted its full-year profit and sales forecasts heading into the crucial holiday season.

title: U.S. Jobless Claims Edge Up to 203,000, Topping Forecasts as Markets Weigh the Fed's Next Move
dek: Initial claims for unemployment benefits rose by 1,000 to 203,000 in the week ended November 14, the Labor Department said Thursday, coming in above economists' forecasts a day after hawkish Federal Reserve minutes.

title: Alibaba Beats Revenue Estimates as AI Cloud Jumps 53%, but Earnings Miss and Cash Burn Widens
dek: Alibaba reported September-quarter revenue of 271.52 billion yuan on Thursday, ahead of estimates, as its AI cloud business surged — but adjusted earnings missed badly and free cash flow turned more deeply negative.

title: Microsoft To Do to Retire in June 2027, With No Free Replacement for Personal Users
dek: The task app will shut down across Windows, Mac, iOS, Android and the web on June 30, 2027, and personal account holders are being told to find another app.

title: Intel Signs First External Customer for 18A as Yields Hit 70%, CEO Says
dek: Intel says a customer has signed up for its most advanced chipmaking process, a milestone for a foundry business that has been fighting to prove it can win outside work.

title: Waymo Pauses Bay Area Robotaxi Service as Flooded Streets Strand Cars
dek: The driverless taxi service suspended rides across the Bay Area on Wednesday after a powerful storm left several of its cars stuck in flooded intersections.

title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Neon, Its Fourth Gemini 4 Model in Seven Weeks
dek: The new model sits between Google's heaviest and fastest AI systems, with a one-million-token context window and pricing aimed at developers building agentic software.

title: Attackers Hijacked Microsoft's AI Agent Package on PyPI to Steal Cloud Credentials
dek: Two poisoned releases of Microsoft's agent-framework package ran a credential stealer every time Python started, even if the package was never imported, before PyPI quarantined them.

title: Ella Langley Sweeps 2026 CMA Awards With Record Six Wins in One Night
dek: The Alabama singer took entertainer of the year and swept the top five major categories at the 60th CMA Awards in Nashville, a night that also featured Taylor Swift's first performance there in 13 years.

title: Grand Theft Auto VI Launches Worldwide With a 99 on Metacritic and $1.65 Billion in Presales
dek: Rockstar's long-awaited sequel went on sale at midnight around the world on Thursday, 13 years after Grand Theft Auto V, to near-perfect reviews and millions of people watching it being played.

title: Fall Out Boy Sells Out Stadium Shows Worldwide as Twilight of the Punks Tour Nears
dek: The band's 2027 world tour has sold out its London stadium, its Chicago homecoming, and the entire UK and Ireland run, with Boston, New York, and Berlin now running low.

title: Billy Crystal's 860 Smashes Imperial Theatre Record for a Play
dek: The solo show grossed $1,720,253 in the week ending November 15, beating the record Crystal himself set with 700 Sundays in 2013.

title: Blue Man Group Brings Holiday Show to Broadway After 33-Year Astor Place Run
dek: Blue Man Group: A New Holiday Surprise opened at the Lunt-Fontanne Theatre on November 17, bringing the blue-painted trio to Broadway for the first time in a limited run through January 3.

title: Nuggets Rally From 17 Down to Edge Celtics 105-101
dek: Denver erased a 17-point first-half deficit behind Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray, then survived a frantic finish to hand Boston its second straight loss.

title: Hawks Top Thunder 117-112 as Former Champs Dort and Wiggins Return to OKC
dek: Atlanta held off Oklahoma City on Wednesday, with Onyeka Okongwu scoring 28 and Jalen Johnson posting a triple-double, in a game defined by two familiar faces on the other side.

title: Pochettino Starts as Manchester United Head Coach Four Days Before Liverpool Trip
dek: Mauricio Pochettino reported for work at Carrington on Wednesday, hours after flying in from the United States, with his first match a trip to Anfield on Sunday.

title: Duckett's 133 Powers England to First ODI Series Win Over Australia in Eight Years
dek: Ben Duckett hit a match-winning century in Hobart as England won the third one-day international by 97 runs to take the series 2-1.

title: Chelsea Beat PSG 1-0 to Top Women's Champions League Table
dek: Veerle Buurman's 87th-minute winner at Plough Lane sent Chelsea top of the league phase and extended their record run of clean sheets in Europe.

title: Voyager 1 Reaches One Light-Day From Earth, a First for Any Human-Made Object
dek: NASA says the probe crossed the milestone at 5:16 a.m. ET on Wednesday, nearly 50 years after launch, and a radio signal now takes a full day to reach it.

title: Huawei Trial Nears Its End as Jury Prepares to Deliberate in Brooklyn
dek: After two months of testimony, prosecutors told jurors the Chinese telecom giant operated as a criminal enterprise for 20 years. The defense said the government started with guilt and worked backwards.

title: Judge Blocks Trump Administration's Limits on Internships for International Students
dek: A federal judge in Boston said the Homeland Security Department likely broke the law when it narrowed a decades-old training program used by more than 140,000 foreign students.

title: Passenger Charged With Attempted Murder After Somali Uber Driver Is Strangled and Run Over in Minnesota
dek: Mohamed Yusuf, 51, is in critical condition with broken ribs, a broken leg, spinal injuries and collapsed lungs. Prosecutors say they cannot prove the attack was motivated by bias.

title: NSA's Classified Internal Network Goes Down in Latest U.S. Tech Outage
dek: The spy agency closed its Fort Meade campus to most employees after its highly classified network went down during a software patch. Officials say there is no evidence of a cyberattack.

title: U.S. Strikes Iran's Qeshm Island as Tehran Hits Back at Bases in Kuwait and Bahrain
dek: The exchange is the widest escalation of the nine-month-old U.S.-Iran war in weeks, with Gulf states intercepting missiles and drones and a Houthi missile aimed at Riyadh.

title: Xi and Putin Rail Against Protectionism and Sanctions as Trump Lands in China for First Three-Way Talks
dek: At the APEC summit in Shenzhen, China's leader pledged to defend free trade and Russia's president attacked Western sanctions, hours before a first-ever trilateral meeting with the U.S. president.

title: Trump's Board of Peace Warns Gaza Ceasefire Is Near Collapse as Israel and Hamas Miss Commitments
dek: A 12-page report to the U.N. Security Council faults both sides, saying a ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained and warning there would be no road map back if it fails.

title: Russian Military Transport Plane Crashes in Siberia, Killing All 19 on Board
dek: The An-12 went down near a village in the Kemerovo region during a scheduled flight. The Defence Ministry said a technical malfunction was the preliminary cause.

title: Category 5 Cyclone Xavier Bears Down on Northern Cook Islands as Shelters Open
dek: The storm, packing sustained winds of about 220 km/h, is passing near Pukapuka and Manihiki. It is expected to stay offshore of inhabited islands but bring damaging seas and flooding rain.

title: Trump Lands in China as Xi and Putin Meet Ahead of First-Ever Trilateral Summit
dek: The president arrived in Shenzhen for the APEC summit, where he will meet Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin together on Thursday to discuss nuclear arms and the war in Ukraine.

title: Peltola Wins Alaska Senate Race, Giving Democrats a 56-44 Majority
dek: The Associated Press called the race Tuesday night, ending a two-week wait and capping a nine-seat Democratic flip in the Senate.

title: Schumer Snaps at Reporters as Van Hollen Challenge Roils Senate Democrats
dek: With the leadership vote set for December 1, the majority leader insists he has the votes while his challenger claims growing support in a secret-ballot contest.

title: The Midterm Blitz That Saved Pete Buttigieg From Quitting Politics
dek: The former transportation secretary campaigned in 38 states for 102 candidates, and now says a second presidential run is very much on his mind.

title: Trump Pulls Vance Off Iran Talks and Sends Him After Fraud in Democratic-Led Cities
dek: The vice president, who led months of negotiations with Tehran, will now focus his complete and total attention on alleged corruption in Democratic-led states.

title: Nvidia Posts Record $115.8 Billion Quarter in First Earnings Without Huang
dek: Revenue more than doubled as AI demand kept climbing, but the chipmaker's new leadership faces questions about circular financing, China probes, and a $518 billion pile of commitments.

title: Target Posts Strongest Sales Gain in Five Years, Helped by a $301 Million Tariff Refund
dek: Net sales rose 7.1% in the third quarter as price cuts and a revamped lineup brought shoppers back, but half of the profit beat came from tariff refunds.

title: Lowe's Beats Earnings Estimates as Online Sales Jump 17.4%
dek: The home improvement retailer raised its full-year outlook, but a $250 million tariff refund did much of the heavy lifting on the bottom line.

title: TJX Rises on Strong Quarter as Bargain Hunters Keep Coming
dek: The off-price retailer beat sales estimates and raised its full-year outlook, with comparable sales up 4% and shares climbing about 6% in premarket trading.

title: Rents Rise for the First Time Since June 2023
dek: The median asking rent ticked up $1 in October as the apartment construction boom fades, but renters still have the upper hand in most big cities.

title: Anthropic IPO Set to Price Above Its $70–$78 Range as Orders Swamp the Offering
dek: The AI company is expected to price its blockbuster offering on Wednesday night, with demand running about seven times the shares on offer and trading set to begin Thursday under the ticker ANT.

title: Microsoft Unveils Seven New MAI Models at Ignite, Taking Aim at Anthropic and OpenAI
dek: The company rolled out coding, cybersecurity, image, voice and routing models at its Ignite conference in San Francisco, claiming near-frontier performance at a fraction of rivals' prices.

title: Apple Says Internal Update — Not a Cyberattack — Knocked Out iCloud, App Store and Apple Pay
dek: A botched internal update disrupted Apple services for hours on Tuesday, signing some users out of their accounts and blocking purchases in stores, the company said.

title: SEC Is Probing Nvidia as Huang's Departure Deepens the Chipmaker's Crisis
dek: The regulator is investigating whether Nvidia's disclosures misled investors, the Wall Street Journal reported, as the board's own inquiry and a Treasury demand for answers pile pressure on the company.

title: Harry Styles, Billie Eilish and Sam Fender to Headline Glastonbury 2027 as Festival Returns
dek: Sam Fender, Harry Styles and Billie Eilish will top the Pyramid Stage bill at Worthy Farm next June, with Cher taking the Sunday Legends slot at 81.

title: GTA VI Leads The Game Awards 2026 With Eight Nominations Two Days Before Launch
dek: Rockstar's sequel picked up eight nominations, including Game of the Year, ahead of its Thursday release — the most of any game this year.

title: Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping Draws Split Reviews Ahead of Friday Release
dek: Critics are split on the sixth Hunger Games film, praising newcomer Joseph Zada as Haymitch while faulting a dragging middle and a rushed ending.

title: Only Murders in the Building Heads to London in Season 6 Trailer
dek: Hulu's hit mystery moves to London for its sixth season, with Tina Fey's Cinda Canning as the victim and Nicola Coughlan as the prime suspect.

title: Netflix Orders Harlan Coben's The Innocent as Its 15th Adaptation of the Author
dek: The streamer ordered a limited series of Coben's 2005 novel at the Texas Book Festival, its 15th adaptation of the author's work.

title: Pistons Snap Spurs' 12-Game Winning Streak With 105–93 Win in San Antonio
dek: Cade Cunningham and Daniss Jenkins combined for 52 points as Detroit rallied from 14 down to end San Antonio's 12-game winning streak.

title: McDavid Ties Gretzky's 23-Game Season-Opening Point Streak as Oilers Beat Panthers 5–2
dek: The Oilers captain tied Gretzky's 1988–89 run and passed him for the franchise power-play points record in a 5–2 win over the Panthers.

title: Zverev Beats Shelton in Straight Sets to Reach ATP Finals Semifinals First
dek: The world No. 1 beat Ben Shelton 6–2, 7–6(4) in Turin, losing just two points on serve in the second set to become the first semifinalist.

title: Grimes' Career-High 47 Lifts Lakers Past Hornets 118–114 in Overtime
dek: Quentin Grimes scored 21 points in the fourth quarter and hit the tying three with two seconds left as the Lakers won their ninth straight game.

title: Gauthier's Record Fourth Hat Trick of November Not Enough as Blues Outgun Ducks 8–6
dek: Cutter Gauthier became the first player in NHL history with four hat tricks in a calendar month, but St. Louis outscored Anaheim 8–6.

title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol, Cutting Prices as the AI Race Tightens
dek: The new models are cheaper and stronger on OpenAI's own tests, but independent measurements found smaller savings than the company claims — and the safety card flags a new concern about the flagship model hiding obstacles from its users.

title: U.S. Intelligence Says Iran Is Drawing Up Plans for a Dirty Bomb Attack in Washington
dek: Seven U.S. officials told CNN that Tehran is developing plans to target senior Trump administration officials with a radiological or chemical weapon in the capital. The White House says there is no credible threat to the homeland right now, and Iran calls the report fabricated.

title: Your TV and Radio Will Interrupt for a Minute Today. It Is Only a Test, and There Is No Blackout Coming.
dek: FEMA and the FCC are running a nationwide test of the Emergency Alert System at about 2:20 p.m. Eastern on Tuesday, November 17. Phones will not buzz, the power grid will not go down, and the viral rumors of a 90-day blackout have no basis in any official announcement.

title: Pentagon Fails Its Financial Audit for the Ninth Year in a Row, Even as Most of Its Units Pass
dek: Independent auditors again could not verify the Defense Department's books for fiscal 2026, issuing another disclaimer of opinion on more than $4.8 trillion in assets. But 14 of the Pentagon's 25 reporting entities passed their own audits, the first time a majority of its assets carried clean opinions.

title: Three Killed After Small Plane Crashes on the Grand Canyon's North Rim
dek: A Piper PA-24 Comanche carrying three people went down on the North Rim of Grand Canyon National Park on Sunday night. Searchers found the wreckage on Monday morning after a nearly 12-hour search. The NTSB is investigating, and the cause is not yet known.

title: Virginia Sen. Louise Lucas Pleads Not Guilty to Federal Racketeering and Drug Charges
dek: Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas pleaded not guilty Monday to federal charges accusing her of leading a marijuana enterprise that prosecutors say made about $4.5 million. Her trial is set for September 13, 2027, and she says she will not resign or give up her Senate leadership post.

title: Ukraine Strike Sends Part of Putin's Bridge to Crimea Into the Sea
dek: Ukraine struck the 19-kilometer bridge linking Russia to occupied Crimea for a second straight day, sending its road arch into the Kerch Strait. Russia answered by hitting Kyiv's two main bridges, as both sides traded their heaviest infrastructure attacks in months.

title: Iran Fires Drones at U.S. Radar in Bahrain; Bahrain Says the Attack Was Intercepted
dek: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said its drones hit a U.S. radar system at the Sheikh Isa base in Bahrain on Tuesday. Bahrain said it intercepted the attack, and U.S. Central Command said no American equipment was damaged and no personnel were hurt.

title: Five EU Countries Unveil Plans for a Rwanda Deportation Hub
dek: Germany, Austria, Denmark, Greece and the Netherlands announced plans on Monday for a joint return hub in Rwanda for rejected asylum seekers, starting with a pilot of about 100 people in 2027. Rights groups condemned the plan, and its backers admit the point is the signal it sends.

title: Japan Scrambles Jets and Protests After Suspected Russian Aircraft Breach Its Airspace
dek: Two aircraft believed to be Russian entered Japanese airspace off Okinoshima Island early on Tuesday, each for about three minutes, prompting Japan to scramble fighter jets and lodge a stern protest with Moscow. Taiwan and South Korea reported encounters with Russian aircraft the same morning.

title: Seventeen Killed in Two Separate Mass Shootings in South Africa
dek: Seventeen people were killed in two separate mass shootings in South Africa on Sunday night — nine in a shack outside Pretoria and eight in a minibus outside Pietermaritzburg. Police say the attacks were unrelated, no arrests have been made, and no motive has been established in either case.

title: Duffy's $50 Billion Air Traffic Ask Meets a Skeptical Congress After Ground Stop Chaos
dek: Days after a nationwide ground stop stranded more than a million passengers, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy is pressing Congress for as much as $50 billion to rebuild air traffic control — and lawmakers in both parties are demanding to know what happened to the last $12.5 billion first.

title: Newly Elected Democrats in Denver Urge Party to Work With Trump, Not Just Investigate Him
dek: At the 'What's Next' conference in Denver, the Democrats who just won the midterms told their party to chase results with President Trump rather than spend two years on investigations — a message that puts them at odds with the party's 'lawyer up' wing.

title: Supreme Court Leaves Maryland's 'Sensitive Places' Gun Law Standing, but Thomas Signals Doubts
dek: The justices declined on Monday to decide whether Maryland can ban guns in stadiums, bars, parks and other 'sensitive places,' leaving the 2023 law in force — while Justice Clarence Thomas wrote that he is skeptical the restrictions are lawful.

title: Supreme Court Turns Away Challenge to How the Federal Judiciary Handles Harassment Complaints
dek: The justices declined on Monday to hear former federal public defender Caryn Strickland's case, leaving in place a system in which the judiciary's 30,000 employees must pursue misconduct complaints through an internal process with no independent decision-maker.

title: Senate Republicans Race to Confirm Trump's Judges, but Their Own Members Are Slowing the Push
dek: With 54 days left in the majority, Senate Republicans have confirmed 58 of President Trump's second-term judicial nominees — but blue-slip fights and objections from departing senators are stalling the final sprint.

title: Wall Street Sinks as Nvidia Rout Drags the Nasdaq Into a Correction
dek: Stocks fell sharply on Monday, with the Nasdaq dropping 2.5 percent and chip stocks plunging ahead of Nvidia's earnings report on Tuesday — the first since its founder resigned.

title: Anthropic Heads Into Its $1.3 Trillion Debut as AI Stocks Wobble
dek: The maker of the Claude AI models is set to price its shares on Wednesday and start trading on the Nasdaq as ANT on Thursday, in what would be one of the largest listings in history — arriving in the middle of a brutal AI sell-off.

title: Nvidia's Vera Rubin Sweeps AI Benchmarks as Partners Ramp Up Shipments
dek: Nvidia's new Vera Rubin platform posted the fastest time on six of seven MLPerf Training benchmarks in its debut, doubling its predecessor's speed on the hardest workload — even as the company's stock reels ahead of Tuesday's earnings report.

title: Fed Minutes Land Wednesday as Traders Bet on Another December Rate Hike
dek: Minutes from the Federal Reserve's October meeting arrive on Wednesday, and investors will comb them for clues about a December rate hike that markets now see as a near certainty.

title: Tyson Shares Jump as the Meatpacker Sees Its Beef Losses Shrinking
dek: Tyson Foods led the S&P 500 on Monday after reporting a fourth-quarter beat and forecasting that its loss-making beef business could approach break-even in fiscal 2027 — even as it warned of lower sales and weaker chicken profits.

title: California Sues OpenAI Over Rogue AI Agents That Attacked Hugging Face
dek: Attorney General Rob Bonta says OpenAI lost control of autonomous agents more than 80 times in testing and told the public about only 27 of them.

title: AMD Closes $8.2 Billion World Labs Deal and Names Fei-Fei Li Chief Scientist
dek: The chipmaker completed its second-largest acquisition ever as it pushes into world models, the AI systems that learn from 3D environments.

title: Google Finds AI Agents Turning Security Patches Into Working Exploits With No Human in the Loop
dek: Google's threat team says it has seen the first fully automated vulnerability discovery and exploitation — a milestone that changes the clock for patching.

title: Apple Tightens Mac Controls to Stop AI Agents Running Amok
dek: macOS 27.3 will split the Mac's most powerful permission in two and force apps to ask every time, after incidents showed AI assistants reaching further than users expected.

title: Robert Pattinson Is the New James Bond
dek: Amazon MGM Studios confirmed the 40-year-old as 007 on Monday, with Denis Villeneuve directing the 26th film in the series.

title: The Odyssey Arrives at Home Today After a Four-Month Theatrical Run
dek: Christopher Nolan's $1.8 billion epic hits digital and disc on Tuesday, 123 days after it opened in cinemas — and returns to IMAX screens in December.

title: Slow Horses Renewed for Seasons 9 and 10 in Apple's Longest Commitment Yet
dek: Apple TV has ordered two more seasons of the spy drama, a day after Olivia Cooke said the cast thought the show was ending.

title: Baby Reindeer Defamation Trial Set for May 18, 2027
dek: A federal judge in Los Angeles set the date for Fiona Harvey's lawsuit against Netflix, rejecting both sides' request for a later start.

title: The Fantasticks Finally Reaches Broadway, 66 Years After It Opened Off-Broadway
dek: The world's longest-running musical opened at the Hayes Theater on Monday with a reimagined romance: boy meets boy.

title: Chargers End 11-Game Losing Streak, Beat Ravens 23-20 on Monday Night
dek: Los Angeles won for the first time in 2026, running for 160 yards while Baltimore's ground game managed just 16.

title: Embiid's Season-High 37 Keeps the 76ers Rolling Past the Nets
dek: Philadelphia improved to 12-3, its best start since 2000-01, while the rest of Monday's NBA slate delivered a Pelicans triple-double record and a Magic upset.

title: Germany Thrash Slovakia 6-0 to Book Their World Cup Place
dek: Leroy Sané scored twice in Leipzig as Germany finished top of Group A, while the Netherlands and Croatia also qualified on Monday.

title: Alcaraz and Medvedev Win Openers as the ATP Finals Get Under Way in Turin
dek: Carlos Alcaraz needed 69 minutes to dismiss Frances Tiafoe, while Daniil Medvedev edged debutant Flavio Cobolli in straight sets.

title: Canucks Snap Seven-Game Skid With 6-3 Win Over the Golden Knights
dek: Filip Chytil scored twice, including a short-handed breakaway, as Vancouver won in regulation for the first time since October 3.

title: Malware Planted Through Optimizely Hit 178 Major Websites, Including Zoom, the BBC and CNN
dek: Visitors to the websites of 178 organisations were served malicious code on Monday after attackers slipped JavaScript into Optimizely's A/B-testing platform, swapping crypto wallet addresses, skimming card details and targeting older iPhones.

title: Tanker Loses Steering and Capsizes Docked New Orleans Riverboat, Sending 32 to Hospital
dek: The tanker Atlantic Asphalt veered across the Mississippi River and struck the American Heritage at its New Orleans dock on Friday, rolling the riverboat onto its side. All 190 people aboard were accounted for, but 32 were taken to hospitals.

title: ULA Vulcan Rocket Fails Minutes After Liftoff, Destroying 40 Amazon Satellites in First Total Loss
dek: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan rocket suffered an anomaly about 10 minutes into Sunday's flight from Cape Canaveral and never reached orbit, wiping out the first 40 satellites of Amazon's Leo broadband network to fly on the new rocket.

title: 50-Foot Waves Batter California Coast as El Niño Supercharges the Surf
dek: The biggest swell in a decade hammered California's coastline over the weekend, flooding streets in Pacifica and Santa Cruz, closing piers from Ventura to San Diego, and sending 50- to 60-foot sets into the famous Mavericks break. Forecasters warn more big surf is coming this week.

title: Trump Administration Gives States Six More Months Before Medicaid Work Requirements Bite
dek: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services told states on Friday they will not have to remove anyone from Medicaid for failing to meet new work requirements until July 1, 2027 — a six-month reprieve for state agencies scrambling to build the systems to enforce the rules.

title: Judge Orders Kim Davis to Explain Hidden Inheritance as $565,000 Judgment Deadline Hits
dek: Former Kentucky county clerk Kim Davis faces a Monday deadline to tell a federal judge why she should not be sanctioned after the court found she gave false answers about an inheritance while owing $565,000 to the gay couple she refused to marry.

title: Congo's Ebola Outbreak Tops 11,000 Cases Six Months In, With No End in Sight
dek: Six months after it was declared, Congo's Ebola outbreak has infected 11,376 people and killed 5,568, and health officials say it is still not under control. Two-thirds of the dead are dying in their communities, not in treatment centres, as conflict and mistrust hamper the response.

title: Spain Heads to Snap Election With Far Right Poised to Enter Government for First Time Since Franco
dek: Spain votes on November 29 in a snap election that could end eight years of socialist rule and bring the far-right Vox party into national government for the first time since the return to democracy. Polls put the People's Party first, but only a deal with Vox gives it a majority.

title: Hundreds of Thousands Fill Prague's Letná Park to Defend Public Media From Government Overhaul
dek: Hundreds of thousands of Czechs filled Prague's Letná Park on Sunday to oppose a government plan to scrap the public broadcasting fee and fund Czech Television and Czech Radio from the state budget — a move critics say would hand politicians control over the media.

title: Estonia to Shut All Russia Border Crossings After Foiled Arson Attack on Drone Maker
dek: Estonia will shut its Narva, Luhamaa and Koidula crossings with Russia from December 1 after officials blamed Moscow's GRU for a foiled arson attack on drone maker Threod Systems. Eight people living in Latvia were detained over the attempt.

title: 'Boss of Bosses' Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, Architect of Mexico's Modern Drug Trade, Dies at 80
dek: Miguel Ángel Félix Gallardo, the founder of the Guadalajara cartel and the man convicted in the 1985 murder of DEA agent Enrique "Kiki" Camarena, died on Sunday in a Guadalajara hospital at 80 after suffering multiple organ failure.

title: China Confirms First-Ever Trump–Xi–Putin Meeting for Thursday in Shenzhen
dek: Beijing confirmed on Monday that the three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit, completing a lineup Washington and Moscow had already announced — with Washington saying Trump will raise nuclear arms reduction, and no deal expected.

title: Peltola's 50% Problem: Why a Lead of 11,213 Votes Has Not Settled Alaska's Senate Race
dek: The Democrat sits at 49.94% on the state's full count and just over 50% on another reading — and the difference comes down to 872 write-in votes and what counts as a majority.

title: Schumer Allies Say He Has the Votes as Van Hollen's Leadership Challenge Tests Senate Democrats
dek: The first contested Senate Democratic leadership race in more than three decades will be decided by secret ballot on December 1, and both camps are counting — in public, at least — while most of the caucus stays quiet.

title: Judge Orders Justice Department to Publish Withheld FBI Notes on Epstein Interviews by November 23
dek: Senior Judge Emmet Sullivan issued three orders on November 9 in the lawsuit enforcing the Epstein files law, giving Attorney General Todd Blanche two weeks to post handwritten interview notes the department had kept out of its public library.

title: House Oversight Report Says Federal Government Failed Epstein Survivors for Decades
dek: The Republican-led committee's 15-month investigation concluded that Epstein's crimes after 2005 could have been prevented, and it called on the Justice Department to re-interview witnesses and give survivors unredacted access to their own records.

title: Taiwan Stocks Plunge 6% as Nvidia Turmoil Sends Asia's Chip Shares Tumbling
dek: The Taiex suffered its second-biggest single-day points drop on record on Monday as the fallout from Jensen Huang's resignation spread across Asia, a day before Nvidia reports its first results without him.

title: Bitcoin Posts Sixth Straight Weekly Loss After Sliding to $62,006 Over the Weekend
dek: The cryptocurrency fell to its lowest since July before recovering to about $64,200 on Monday, as a seventh straight day of ETF outflows and a fully priced December rate hike kept sellers in control.

title: Nvidia Reports Its First Results Without Huang on Tuesday. Kress Faces the Credibility Test.
dek: Interim chief Colette Kress will present numbers she set as chief financial officer, with analysts expecting about $109 billion in revenue — but the market wants to know whether the outlook for next year survives the leadership change.

title: Oil Slips as IEA Sees a Supply Surplus, Even as Hormuz Attacks Continue
dek: Brent eased to about $95 a barrel on Monday after the International Energy Agency said the world oil market returns to surplus this quarter, with shipments through the Strait of Hormuz nearly back to pre-war levels.

title: Baidu's AI Cloud Nearly Doubles as Search Ads Slide 22%
dek: The Chinese search giant reported third-quarter results on Monday showing its AI business now makes up more than half of its core revenue — but heavy spending on data centers pushed free cash flow into negative territory.

title: Alibaba Launches Qwen4-Max, Its New Flagship AI Model, With a 1-Million-Token Context
dek: Alibaba has launched Qwen4-Max, the flagship of its next-generation Qwen family, with a 1-million-token context window and a public pay-as-you-go API priced below its predecessor.

title: Four Nonprofits Sue OpenAI, Google, Anthropic, Meta and SpaceX to Freeze Frontier AI
dek: Four nonprofits have asked a San Francisco court to freeze frontier AI development at Anthropic, Google, Meta, OpenAI and SpaceX, arguing the companies are building systems they admit they cannot control.

title: Microsoft Says Next Xbox Project Helix Plays PC Games but Is Not a PC
dek: In its 25th anniversary magazine, Microsoft says its next Xbox, code-named Project Helix, is a console that can also play PC games, not a PC that can also play console games.

title: GDC Survey: 40% of Game Professionals Now Use Generative AI, but 55% Say It Hurts the Industry
dek: A survey of more than 2,600 game industry professionals finds 40 percent now use generative AI at work, up from 36 percent, while 55 percent say it is hurting the industry.

title: Apple Launches Health AI Study of Up to 200,000 iPhone Users With OpenEvidence
dek: Apple has opened the Apple Health AI Usage Study to up to 200,000 iPhone users in the United States, working with clinical AI company OpenEvidence to examine how people trust, understand and act on AI health answers.

title: Glenn Close, Ridley Scott and Floyd Norman Honored at 2026 Governors Awards
dek: Glenn Close finally holds an Oscar after eight nominations without a win, Ridley Scott accepts from afar in tribute to his late brother Tony, and Disney pioneer Floyd Norman gets his happy ending at the Academy's 17th Governors Awards.

title: Raye Leads 2027 Grammy Nominations With 11 as Taylor Swift Earns Five
dek: Raye leads the field for the 69th Grammy Awards with 11 nominations, ahead of Rosalía with nine, as Taylor Swift breaks Frank Sinatra's album of the year record and the nominations are announced live on Monday morning.

title: Johnny Depp's Ebenezer Tops Box Office With $19 Million Opening
dek: Johnny Depp's Ebenezer opens at No. 1 with an estimated $19 million domestically and $42 million worldwide, giving the actor his first chart-topping opening in eight years.

title: Netflix Renews Virgin River for Season 9, Its Longest-Running Scripted Series
dek: Netflix has renewed Virgin River for a ninth season months before Season 8 premieres in 2027, making the romantic drama the streamer's longest-running original scripted series.

title: Carmelle Wins First Eurovision Song Contest Asia for the Philippines
dek: Nineteen-year-old Carmelle Collado wins the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia in Bangkok with her dance-pop anthem Sobra-Sobra, scoring 211 points to finish 41 clear of host country Thailand.

title: Purdy Throws for Career-High 389 Yards as 49ers Outlast Cowboys 46-40
dek: Brock Purdy threw for a career-high 389 yards and three touchdowns, and Christian McCaffrey scored three times, as the San Francisco 49ers held off a furious Dallas rally to win a 46-40 shootout at AT&T Stadium on Sunday.

title: Burrow Throws for 409 Yards and Four Touchdowns as Bengals Rout Steelers 38-18
dek: Joe Burrow passed for 409 yards and four touchdowns, Ja'Marr Chase caught 11 passes for 231 yards, and the Cincinnati Bengals beat the Pittsburgh Steelers 38-18 on Sunday Night Football to take sole possession of first place in the AFC North.

title: Cousins Stars in Emotional Vikings Return as Minnesota Routs Packers 30-10
dek: Kirk Cousins threw two touchdown passes in his first start back with Minnesota, and the Vikings' defense sacked Jordan Love eight times and forced four turnovers in a 30-10 win over the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field.

title: Gibbs Piles Up 252 Total Yards as Lions Roll Patriots 35-10 in Munich
dek: Jahmyr Gibbs ran for 153 yards and two touchdowns and caught seven passes for 99 more as the Detroit Lions beat the New England Patriots 35-10 at Allianz Arena in Munich, extending their winning streak to five games.

title: Tatum Scores 32 as Celtics Rout Mavericks; Lakers and Rockets Roll on Sunday
dek: Jayson Tatum scored 32 points as the Boston Celtics blew out the Dallas Mavericks 131-94, Luka Doncic poured in 43 as the Los Angeles Lakers held off the Phoenix Suns 131-123, and the Houston Rockets routed the Washington Wizards 147-119 on Sunday night.

title: Faulty Router Installed by L3Harris Likely Caused Nationwide FAA Ground Stop, Duffy Says
dek: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said a router installed during a routine copper-to-fibre upgrade flooded air traffic control networks, grounding flights across the country for nearly five hours on Friday.

title: Bessent Publicly Blames Lutnick for Failing to Blacklist Nvidia Chip Buyer Megaspeed
dek: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said four parts of the government wanted the Singapore firm at the centre of the Nvidia spy scandal put on a U.S. trade blacklist, but that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's department never acted.

title: U.S. Loses Measles Elimination Status After 26 Years as Cases Hit Highest Level Since 1991
dek: The Pan American Health Organization has determined the United States no longer qualifies as having eliminated measles, after the same strain of the virus circulated without a break for more than a year.

title: U.S. Floated Trading Donbas for NATO Membership, Zelensky Says
dek: President Volodymyr Zelensky said American negotiators asked for the first time whether Ukraine would withdraw from the Donbas in exchange for joining NATO, and that he would put any such deal to a national referendum.

title: At Least 38 Killed in Ambush on Market Convoy in Western Niger
dek: Gunmen ambushed villagers travelling to a weekly market in the Tillaberi region, killing 37 people at the scene, local sources told AFP. A further victim died of wounds on Friday.

title: COP31 Enters Final Week With Fossil Fuel Divide Unresolved, Climate Chief Warns
dek: UN climate chief Simon Stiell urged negotiators in Antalya to move swiftly to the hardest issues and avoid tactical delays, as big fossil fuel producers resist any deal with firm new targets.

title: ASEAN Summit Opens in Manila With Energy, South China Sea and Myanmar on the Agenda
dek: Southeast Asian leaders opened the 49th ASEAN Summit on Sunday for three days of talks, with President Donald Trump due to arrive on Tuesday for meetings with the bloc and the Quad.

title: Three Oil Tankers Catch Fire After Striking Mines in the Strait of Hormuz
dek: Iran said three tankers hit naval mines on Saturday in the latest attack on shipping through the strait, as Gulf markets fell and a Saudi-led coalition said it downed missiles fired at Riyadh.

title: Trump, Xi and Putin to Hold First-Ever Three-Way Meeting in China Next Week
dek: The White House says the three leaders will meet Thursday on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen to discuss nuclear arms reductions and the war with Iran, though officials expect no agreement.

title: New York Democratic Socialists Urge Ocasio-Cortez to Run for President in 2028
dek: The New York City chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America voted 291-123 on Saturday to urge Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez to seek the White House, the latest push from the left for a 2028 bid.

title: Judge Blocks Trump From Closing Washington's East Potomac Golf Course
dek: U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued a temporary restraining order on Saturday halting the planned 15-month closure of the historic public course, calling the administration's safety rationale 'pretextual.'

title: Peltola's Lead Grows to 11,213 Votes in Alaska as Saturday Count Nears a Majority
dek: Official results released Saturday show the Democrat at 49.94 percent, 157 votes short of a majority, with ranked-choice tabulation set for Wednesday.

title: Van Hollen Pledges to End the Filibuster as Schumer Allies Predict 40-Plus Votes
dek: At a Denver conference on Friday, Van Hollen promised to scrap the 60-vote threshold, ruled out a 2028 White House bid, and picked up Jeff Merkley's endorsement as Schumer's allies predicted a win.

title: Bitcoin Crashes Below $70,000 and Sinks Toward $62,000 in Brutal Weekend Sell-Off
dek: The cryptocurrency fell below $70,000 on Friday and hit a low of $62,081 on Sunday, down about 23 percent from its November 4 high, as ETF outflows and forced selling piled up.

title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Jumps to 5.15% as Hot Inflation Locks In a December Fed Hike
dek: The benchmark yield hit its highest close since mid-October after producer prices rose 6.5 percent from a year earlier, leaving traders pricing in a near-certain rate hike next month.

title: Japan's Nikkei Posts Its Best Week in Five Months as AI Optimism Returns
dek: The Nikkei 225 gained 6.46 percent on the week, its largest rise since June, as chip stocks rebounded on renewed artificial intelligence optimism.

title: Asda Returns to Food Sales Growth as New Chief Potts Takes the Wheel
dek: The supermarket group reported third-quarter revenue up 3.1 percent to £6.5 billion, with food sales back in growth, as former Morrisons boss David Potts takes over as chief executive.

title: On Holding Posts Record Third-Quarter Sales as Asia-Pacific Jumps 31%
dek: The Swiss running-shoe maker reported its first quarter above CHF 900 million in sales, with record margins and a raised outlook, even as its shares slid more than 10 percent in a week.

title: Tesla Opens Cybercab Orders at $29,990, but the Car Won't Move Without a $299 Monthly Fee
dek: Tesla has started inviting select customers to order its steering-wheel-free Cybercab for personal use, but the $29,990 two-seater only works inside the company's robotaxi zones and needs a $299-a-month subscription to drive at all — a price Elon Musk himself called too high.

title: Microsoft Says Global Microsoft 365 Outage Is Over After More Than a Day Offline
dek: Microsoft said on Saturday that its Microsoft 365 services were fully restored after a worldwide outage that knocked out Outlook, Teams and Copilot for more than 24 hours, blaming a problem introduced during a network capacity upgrade and ruling out a cyberattack.

title: Intel Stages Surprise Desktop CPU Comeback as AMD Falls Below 30%
dek: Intel reclaimed 70.1% of desktop CPU shipments in the third quarter of 2026, a five-point swing that caught the market off guard — even as overall PC chip shipments shrank and AMD kept gaining ground in servers.

title: Musk Warns Nvidia Could Lose Critical Deals After Huang's Exit: Many Were a Handshake
dek: Elon Musk warned on Saturday that Nvidia could lose some of its most important supply-chain relationships after Jensen Huang's resignation, saying many of the deals were sealed with a handshake rather than a written contract.

title: Judge Refuses to Dismiss DRAM Lawsuit Against Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron
dek: A federal judge ruled on Friday that a class-action lawsuit accusing Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron of conspiring to restrict memory supply and inflate prices can proceed, rejecting the companies' argument that the case was a rerun of one thrown out in 2022.

title: Phil Collins in Tears as Rock Hall Inducts 2026 Class in Los Angeles
dek: Phil Collins wept at a standing ovation as he was inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame for his solo career on Saturday night, joining a class that also included Billy Idol, Wu-Tang Clan, Luther Vandross and Queen Latifah.

title: John Mulaney Roasts RFK Jr. and Tech Billionaires in Seventh SNL Hosting Turn
dek: John Mulaney hosted Saturday Night Live for a seventh time on Saturday, opening with a CIA sketch about tech billionaires and spies and welcoming Phoebe Bridgers for two songs in the last show before Thanksgiving.

title: Spider-Man and BTS Sweep the 2026 Kids' Choice Awards
dek: Spider-Man: Brand New Day won four movie prizes and BTS took three music awards at the 2026 Kids' Choice Awards on Saturday night, the first to air simultaneously on CBS and Nickelodeon.

title: Ramayana Passes ₹1,200 Crore Worldwide and Overtakes Jawan in 10 Days
dek: Ramayana – Part I passed ₹1,200 crore worldwide in just ten days, overtaking the lifetime totals of Jawan and KGF: Chapter 2 to become the fifth-biggest Indian film of all time.

title: Depp's Ebenezer Eyes $20 Million Opening as How to Rob a Bank Flops
dek: Johnny Depp's Ebenezer is projected for a $20 million opening weekend at the top of the North American box office, while How to Rob a Bank is heading for a $4.7 million flop and Godzilla Minus Zero has fallen 75% in its second weekend.

title: Grant Wilson Throws Two Touchdowns as No. 6 Indiana Beats No. 15 USC 27-13
dek: Grant Wilson threw two touchdown passes in his first start for No. 6 Indiana as the Hoosiers beat No. 15 USC 27-13 on Saturday, surviving three fourth-quarter scares to keep their College Football Playoff hopes alive.

title: Arch Manning Redeems Three Interceptions With Last-Seconds Touchdown as Texas Edges LSU 22-21
dek: Arch Manning threw three interceptions, then found Raleek Brown for a 4-yard touchdown in the final seconds as No. 8 Texas beat LSU 22-21 at Tiger Stadium on Saturday night.

title: Nate Frazier Scores Three Times as No. 1 Georgia Cruises Past Missouri 48-21
dek: Nate Frazier scored three touchdowns as No. 1 Georgia scored on its first five possessions and cruised past No. 22 Missouri 48-21 on Saturday in front of a sellout crowd of 93,033.

title: Tyrese Proctor's First Triple-Double Lifts Shorthanded Cavaliers Past Mavericks 127-117
dek: Tyrese Proctor recorded his first career triple-double as the shorthanded Cleveland Cavaliers, missing their entire starting five, stunned the Dallas Mavericks 127-117 on Saturday night.

title: Scheifele Makes Franchise History as Jets Rally From 4-0 Down to Beat Blackhawks 5-4 in Shootout
dek: Mark Scheifele passed Dale Hawerchuk as the franchise's all-time leading scorer as the Winnipeg Jets rallied from 4-0 down to beat the Chicago Blackhawks 5-4 in a shootout on Saturday.

title: Eight Dead in Brooklyn Building Collapse as City Widens Inspections to 160 Sites
dek: A three-story building in Brooklyn's Flatbush neighborhood fell into a construction excavation on Wednesday, killing eight people including two children. The city has now ordered inspections at about 160 sites tied to the project, and the Brooklyn district attorney has opened a criminal probe.

title: Wildfires Are Poisoning America's Drinking Water for Years After the Flames Go Out
dek: New studies show that wildfire contamination can linger in the rivers and streams that supply drinking water for more than a decade. With more than 68,000 fires burning over 14,062 square miles in the U.S. so far in 2026, water utilities are scrambling to adapt.

title: FAA Lifts Nationwide Ground Stop After Communications Outage Strands Thousands
dek: The Federal Aviation Administration ended a nationwide halt to departures on Friday night after an air traffic control communications failure grounded flights across the country for more than four hours.

title: Supreme Court Agrees to Decide Whether Trump Can Bar Asylum at the Southern Border
dek: The justices will review the border asylum ban President Trump imposed on his first day back in office, in a case that could define how far presidential power reaches over the asylum system.

title: An 8-Year-Old Went to an ICE Check-In With His Uncle. He Left in Federal Custody.
dek: The Haitian third-grader was separated from the uncle who had raised him since his father's deportation, and his school district says it still does not know where he is being held.

title: Winter Heating Bills Will Rise 7% Nationwide, With Heating Oil Costs Up 70%
dek: A new forecast says the average household will pay $1,002 to heat its home this winter, and families in the Northeast who rely on heating oil face bills of nearly $3,000.

title: Back-to-Back Atmospheric Rivers Bring Heavy Rain and Monster Surf to the Pacific Northwest
dek: Two more rivers in the sky will soak Oregon and Washington this weekend after two earlier storms dumped inches of rain, with 20-foot swells and king tides raising the flood risk.

title: Ukraine Fires Nearly 1,200 Drones at Russia in One of Its Biggest Attacks of the War
dek: Kyiv's overnight barrage came as U.S.-led talks widened to include European security, and as Russia's own drones killed civilians in Odesa, Zaporizhzhia and Kyiv.

title: Turkey and Qatar Sign Mutual Defence Pact Pledging a United Front Against Attack
dek: The agreement, signed in Istanbul by President Erdogan and Qatar's emir, commits the two countries to consult on security threats and expand joint military exercises and defence-industry ties.

title: China Stages Unannounced Pacific Drills Around Taiwan, Taipei Says
dek: Taiwan says more than 100 Chinese naval and coast guard vessels massed around the island in early November, in drills its defence minister calls 'area denial' exercises.

title: IAEA Says It Cannot Locate Iran's Uninspected Isfahan Enrichment Plant or Its Uranium
dek: The UN nuclear watchdog says it does not know where the Isfahan Fuel Enrichment Plant is, whether it holds nuclear material, or the fate of Iran's stockpile of near-weapons-grade uranium.

title: Houthis Claim Drone and Missile Attacks on Saudi Oil Pipeline, Yanbu and Riyadh
dek: Yemen's Houthis say they hit a pumping station on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and an oil facility in Yanbu, as the kingdom's Hormuz bypass becomes a target in the widening Gulf war.

title: Peltola's Lead Nearly Doubles in Alaska as Friday Count Puts Her at 49.84%
dek: Mary Peltola added more than 13,000 votes in Friday's update, stretching her lead over Sen. Dan Sullivan to 10,412 votes — but she remains just short of the majority that would settle the race outright.

title: Congress Summons Huang and Lutnick as Nvidia Spy Scandal Reaches Capitol Hill
dek: Senate Banking Chairman Tim Scott wants the former Nvidia chief on December 3 and the commerce secretary on December 10, with subpoenas threatened if either refuses.

title: Blanche Walks It Back: No Criminal Probes of Democrats Over Oversight Threats
dek: The attorney general said Thursday the Justice Department has no active criminal investigations into lawmakers' words, days after suggesting oversight threats 'could be' a crime.

title: Boebert Ousted: Laubacher Flips Colorado's Reddest Seat
dek: Democrat Eileen Laubacher defeated three-term Rep. Lauren Boebert 48.8% to 47.9% in a district Donald Trump carried by 18 points, capping a brutal midterm for House Republicans.

title: Stocks End Mixed Friday but Wall Street Still Notches a Winning Week
dek: The S&P 500 slipped 0.4% and the Nasdaq fell 0.9% as chip stocks gave back Thursday's gains, but all three major indexes still finished the week higher.

title: Samsung in Talks to Buy Modine in $7.5 Billion AI Cooling Bet
dek: Modine shares soared 28% after Bloomberg reported the talks; a deal would be the biggest acquisition in Samsung's history.

title: Cerebras Lands Microsoft as Record Quarter Beats Expectations
dek: Core revenue jumped 70% to $230.9 million and the AI chipmaker raised its full-year outlook, naming Microsoft as its third hyperscaler customer.

title: Oil Holds Near $96 as Hormuz Attacks and Trump's Iran Snub Keep Traders on Edge
dek: Brent settled at $95.84 after a week of tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz, even as the IEA said the market will be in surplus this quarter.

title: Virgin Galactic Crashes 31% as $250 Million Stock Sale Spooks Investors
dek: Shares fell to $1.84 after the space tourism company said it would sell up to $250 million of stock and pushed its first commercial flight to early 2027.

title: Appeals Court Blocks Trump's $73.5 Million Highway Funding Cut to New York
dek: The Second Circuit ruled the Transportation Department overstepped its authority by punishing New York for licenses issued under rules that never required expiration dates to match drivers' immigration documents.

title: Tesla's Cybertruck Wind-Down Accelerates as Only the $109,990 Cyberbeast Remains on Sale
dek: Tesla has pulled every cheaper Cybertruck from its U.S. configurator and dropped its lowest-priced Model Y, as the company clears the decks for its robotaxi.

title: SpaceX to Spend Over $74 Billion on AI Supercomputing Campuses in Texas and Arizona
dek: The rocket company is pivoting hard into artificial intelligence infrastructure, with two mega-campuses that together would create more than 9,500 construction jobs.

title: OpenAI Launches ChatGPT Wallet, Letting AI Agents Pay for Your Purchases
dek: The new wallet lets ChatGPT's shopping agents check out on your behalf, using a payment token instead of your real card number.

title: Fed Survey: AI Now the Top-Cited Risk to the Financial System
dek: Eighty-seven percent of market contacts named artificial intelligence as a salient risk in the Federal Reserve's latest Financial Stability Report, up from 50 percent in May.

title: LangChain Raises $300 Million at a $3 Billion Valuation
dek: The AI agent startup more than doubled its valuation in about a year as demand for tools that build and run agents keeps climbing.

title: "Ebenezer" Tops Friday Box Office as Johnny Depp Scores First No. 1 in Eight Years
dek: The dark Dickens retelling earned $7.1 million on Friday and is pacing for a $20 million-plus opening, Depp's first No. 1 since 2018.

title: Rock Hall Induction Set for Saturday as Oasis, Sade and Iron Maiden Skip the Stage
dek: Oasis, Sade and Iron Maiden will all miss Saturday's ceremony at the Peacock Theater, leaving Wu-Tang Clan, Billy Idol and Queen Latifah to carry the night.

title: John Mulaney Hosts "SNL" for a Seventh Time With Phoebe Bridgers as Musical Guest
dek: The comedian's seventh hosting turn airs Saturday at 11:30 p.m. ET, with Phoebe Bridgers performing songs from her August album "Lost Weekend."

title: Jessica Chastain's Country-Music Mystery "Heartland" Arrives on Netflix
dek: Chastain stars as a disgraced former country singer who returns to Nashville after her niece disappears in Shana Feste's mystery thriller.

title: "Avatar: Fire and Ash" Collector's Edition Arrives December 8 With 12 Deleted Scenes
dek: The December 8 set includes 12 deleted scenes, more than nine hours of extras and a two-part making-of documentary.

title: Spurs Rout Warriors 123-85 for 11th Straight Win
dek: Stephon Castle scored a season-high 32 points as San Antonio opened the game on an 18-0 run and never looked back.

title: Garland's Late Three-Point Play Lifts Clippers Past Thunder 113-112
dek: Garland's driving three-point play capped a late 7-0 run as the Clippers stunned the short-handed Thunder.

title: Sengun's 43 Powers Rockets Past Jazz 125-118
dek: Sengun scored a season-high 43 points and teamed with Kevin Durant for 65 as Houston sent Utah to its 11th straight loss.

title: Adebayo and Giannis Score 37 Each as Heat Beat Cavaliers 133-121
dek: Adebayo and Antetokounmpo combined for 74 points and joined LeBron James and Dwyane Wade as the only Heat duos to each score 35-plus in the same game.

title: Bulls Snap Eight-Game Skid With 125-117 Overtime Win Over Hawks
dek: Powell scored 33 in his return and Josh Giddey posted a triple-double as Chicago ended an eight-game losing streak in overtime.

title: ICE Deported a Record 483,200 People in Fiscal 2026 as Arrests Also Hit a High
dek: The Department of Homeland Security says immigration enforcement set agency records on both fronts in the year that ended September 30 — though independent data shows much of the deportation total came from voluntary departures, not formal removals.

title: FBI Claws Back $1.2 Billion From the Binance Hack and Exposes North Korea's FaceStealer Con
dek: The Justice Department won court orders covering more than $1.2 billion stolen from the world's largest crypto exchange, and seized the cloud servers behind a fake video-call scheme that has taken more than $400 million.

title: Doctor Kills Building Manager in D.C. Gym, Wounds Four, Then Takes His Own Life
dek: Police say a 55-year-old emergency physician shot the manager of his condominium building inside a Logan Circle gym, then fired on people in the street from his seventh-floor balcony before barricading himself inside.

title: First Big Winter Storm of the Season Brings Up to Two Feet of Snow to the Sierra
dek: Winter storm warnings cover the Sierra Nevada from Friday morning to Saturday morning, with a foot of snow expected around Lake Tahoe and up to two feet on the crest, while a series of Pacific storms brings rain and huge surf to the California coast.

title: Trump Threatens to Double Tariffs on Mexico Over Migrant Caravan Heading North
dek: The president warned that tariffs on Mexico will be immediately doubled if the country does not stop a caravan of about 1,500 migrants that set out from Tapachula on Tuesday.

title: Iran Claims It Hit a U.S. Radar in Bahrain as a Tanker Strikes a Mine in Hormuz
dek: The Revolutionary Guard said it destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain and that a gas tanker hit a mine in the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. military said it shot down two Iranian drones headed for Bahrain and denied the radar claim.

title: Europe Gets a Seat at the Next Ukraine Peace Talks as Envoys Push a Record Prisoner Swap
dek: U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner shuttled from Moscow to Dublin this week, and both sides agreed to bring European partners into the next round and to work toward the war's largest prisoner exchange.

title: Pakistan Says Its Forces Killed 74 Militants in Raids Along the Afghan Border
dek: Pakistan's military said 74 militants were killed in intelligence-based operations in Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, including 31 in the Kurram area of Quetta district and 43 in the northwest over the past 48 hours.

title: Car Bomb in Moscow Wounds Ex-Aide to Ukraine's Former Pro-Russian Premier
dek: Sergei Zavorotniy, a former spokesman for exiled Ukrainian prime minister Mykola Azarov, was hospitalized after the car he was driving exploded in Moscow's Chertanovo district, a day after a car bomb killed a serviceman in St. Petersburg.

title: Russian Court Jails Rights Lawyer Maria Bontsler for 12 Years on Treason Charge
dek: Maria Bontsler, 66, was sentenced to 12 years in prison for treason in a closed trial in Kaliningrad. Her lawyers say the case was based on Telegram correspondence that contained nothing secret.

title: Van Hollen Challenges Schumer for Senate Majority Leader in First Contested Race in Decades
dek: Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen announced he will challenge Chuck Schumer to lead Senate Democrats, saying voters called for new leadership after the midterm sweep.

title: Peltola's Lead Grows to 5,800 Votes in Alaska's Uncalled Senate Race as Judge Rejects Ballot-List Request
dek: Democrat Mary Peltola extended her lead over Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in the latest count, while a state judge ruled her campaign cannot get a list of rejected absentee voters mid-count.

title: Trump Sends Bipartisan SEC and CFTC Nominations to the Senate in First Picks in a Year
dek: The White House named two Democrats and two Republicans to the market regulators, filling seats that have sat empty for months as the lame-duck clock runs down.

title: Trump Authorized a Crackdown on Nvidia Chip Diversions Three Times. Lutnick Never Carried It Out, Axios Reports
dek: Axios reports the president approved action against suspected diversions of advanced AI chips to China in May, August and November — and that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick stalled each time.

title: Epstein Files Vote Could Come as Soon as Dec. 2, After Thanksgiving Recess
dek: The discharge petition for a second Epstein files bill reached 218 signatures this week. Under House rules, the earliest floor action would come right after the Thanksgiving break.

title: Jensen Huang Resigns as Nvidia Chief, Ending 33 Years at the Top of the AI Boom
dek: The co-founder who built Nvidia into the world's most valuable company stepped down amid an affair scandal linked to a suspected Chinese spy, and shares fell sharply.

title: Anthropic IPO Orders Run Six Times the Shares on Offer, With Existing Backers First in Line
dek: The AI startup's blockbuster listing is about six times oversubscribed, and bankers are telling new buyers to expect smaller allocations than they asked for.

title: Producer Prices Rose 0.3% in October as Annual Inflation Hit a Four-Year High of 6.5%
dek: The monthly rise was smaller than expected, but the year-over-year rate climbed to its highest since November 2022 — the last major inflation report before the Fed's December meeting.

title: Cisco Posts a Record Quarter as AI Networking Demand Lifts Revenue 24%
dek: The networking giant reported its strongest revenue and earnings growth in more than 15 years and raised its full-year guidance, as hyperscalers buy more gear to connect AI data centers.

title: Microsoft 365 Outage Knocks Out Outlook, Teams and Copilot for a Second Day
dek: A failure that began Thursday afternoon left millions unable to reach email, chat and cloud apps, and Microsoft said Friday morning that service was still degraded as engineers worked to restore capacity.

title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Its Fastest AI Model Yet, in Search and Its Apps
dek: The new model is built for coding and everyday agent work, priced at $1.50 per million input tokens, and Google says it finishes tasks two and a half times faster than its predecessor.

title: Notion Says Fireworks Breach Exposed Some Customers' AI Chat Transcripts
dek: The workspace company told users that transcripts from fewer than 1 percent of workspaces were caught up in a breach at its AI infrastructure provider, and urged affected customers to rotate any credentials shared in chats.

title: 'How to Rob a Bank' Opens in Theaters With Hoult and Kravitz Leading a Viral Heist Crew
dek: David Leitch's new heist thriller follows social-media-savvy robbers who broadcast their jobs to millions. It opens Friday in the U.S. and the U.K.

title: 'Ramayana' Crosses ₹1,000 Crore Worldwide in Eight Days
dek: Nitesh Tiwari's epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor as Lord Rama, is the 11th Indian film to join the ₹1,000-crore club — and it passed the lifetime domestic totals of 'Pathaan' and 'Animal' in just over a week.

title: 'Avengers: Endgame Encore' Arrives on Disney+ With New Scenes Pointing to 'Doomsday'
dek: The extended cut of the 2019 blockbuster, with four new post-credits scenes, streams Friday — and it has already pushed the film back past 'Avatar' as the highest-grossing movie of all time.

title: 'The End of Oak Street' Hits HBO Max After a $121 Million Theatrical Run
dek: Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor star as parents whose suburban street is torn from 1982 Michigan and dropped into a prehistoric world. The film streams Friday on HBO Max.

title: BBC Children in Need 2026 Telethon Airs Tonight With a Star-Studded Line-Up
dek: The 47th annual appeal, hosted from MediaCityUK in Salford, runs from 7 p.m. on BBC One and iPlayer, with the year's fundraising challenges — including a 400-mile cycle ride — reaching their finish lines live on air.

title: Cade Cunningham Drops Career-High 52 as Pistons Outlast Wizards 144–140 in Double Overtime
dek: The Detroit star scored 30 of his 52 points in the fourth quarter and the overtimes, becoming the first player in nearly 50 years with 50 points, 10 assists and no turnovers in a game.

title: Jets Score Five in the Second Period to Rout the Stars 8–3
dek: Winnipeg erased a two-goal deficit with a five-goal middle frame in Dallas, winning a fifth straight game as Mark Scheifele tied Dale Hawerchuk's franchise points record.

title: Matt Boldy's Hat Trick Powers Wild Past Maple Leafs 5–2
dek: Boldy's sixth career hat trick, completed early in the third period, extended Minnesota's point streak to 10 games and handed Toronto a fifth straight loss.

title: Commanders Stun Giants 24–21 on Diggs' Late Touchdown
dek: Jayden Daniels found Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard score with 57 seconds left, and Rasul Douglas sealed it with an interception, as Washington kept its season alive on Thursday Night Football.

title: Pegula Saves Match Point to Beat Noskova and Reach WTA Finals Semifinals
dek: Jessica Pegula won the final three games to beat Linda Noskova 7–6, 4–6, 7–5 in Indian Wells, knocking out Coco Gauff and booking a semifinal against Mirra Andreeva.

title: TSMC Posts Record October Revenue of $17.88 Billion as AI Chip Demand Keeps Climbing
dek: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. reported its biggest month ever in October, with revenue up nearly 60 percent from a year earlier, days after a chip sell-off rattled the market.

title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Security Flaws, Including a 22-Year-Old Bug That Lets a Low-Privilege User Run Code
dek: The open-source database's November update fixes dozens of flaws that could let an ordinary database account run code on the server, and it marks the end of the line for PostgreSQL 14.

title: Nebius Bets $40 Billion on a 2027 Data Center Buildout It Plans to Pay For With Customer Cash
dek: The AI cloud company told investors it will spend $40 billion to $45 billion building data centers next year, funded mostly by customer prepayments, even as delays at its biggest customer's site push revenue into 2027.

title: Eight Dead, 19 Hurt as Brooklyn Building Collapses Into Construction Pit
dek: A three-story building in Flatbush fell into an excavation pit next door on Wednesday afternoon. As of Thursday morning, eight people were confirmed dead and 19 injured, and rescuers warned the toll could still rise.

title: SS United States Sinks Off Florida to Become the World's Largest Artificial Reef
